key_insight: FREDI jointly optimizes fair edge resources and dual-threshold early-exit inference so secure critical-event detection stays accurate while improving UE fairness and utility.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives a tractable way to manage bandwidth, power, association, and inference thresholds in cooperative UE–edge–cloud systems under security and scalability constraints.
method: Proportional-fair utility maximization across UE–ES association, wireless resources, and processing resources
Dual-threshold early-exit CNN screening at each UE with critical events securely offloaded for edge-side refinement
Exact threshold search over a finite confidence domain plus mixed-integer exponential-cone resource allocation with certified optimality gap
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 show near-perfect UE fairness, utility close to a sum-utility benchmark, and Stage-A scaling from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve time below 0.1 s.
watch_item: Security-driven offloading can fragment resources, so performance depends on how well the optimization and threshold settings adapt to changing traffic and confidence distributions.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
